boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Waynesborough record (December 4, 1864) in the Savannah Campaign [November-December 1864]. Buck Head Creek (GA026, November 28) and the December 2-3 skirmishes at Rocky Creek and Thomas' Station precede it. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text names Kilpatrick's division against the cavalry command of the Army of Tennessee, with no numbers; the live field reads zeros. Kilpatrick moved in advance of Baird's infantry division and says Wheeler's corps consisted of four divisions and two independent brigades 'as has since been ascertained'. Wheeler says the enemy cavalry was at least double his numbers and reinforced by one or more infantry divisions, that most of his command had gone three miles for forage, and that 'their long lines of infantry advanced'.
claims.rationale: Formations and relative claims only; the two commanders disagree on whether infantry attacked. Kilpatrick's November 14 strength is recorded in the Buck Head Creek dossier (GA026). None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Kilpatrick says the town was gained and Wheeler's entire force completely routed and pursued eight miles to Brier Creek; Wheeler says he was compelled to fall back by successive positions and withdrew from the town with difficulty, but that a counter-charge stopped further pursuit.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The commanders' characterizations differ.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 440 (US 190; CS 250). Kilpatrick says upward of 200 Confederate wounded left in his hands were wounded by the saber alone and refers his own casualties to a separate report; his provost-marshal lists 550 small-arms captured at Waynesborough on December 4. Wheeler says the Union loss 'according to his own account' was 50 killed and 147 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Wheeler's figure is secondhand; Kilpatrick's casualty report is not printed with his report.

open_questions: Baird's No. 75 report, Atkins's No. 150, Murray's No. 144 and the regimental reports, Kilpatrick's nominal casualty list, Allen's, Humes's and Dibrell's reports, and Cox's Waynesborough passage (p.34, read, not selected) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. C. R. Woods's, G. W. Smith's, Kilpatrick's, Wheeler's, J. P. Hatch's and Hazen's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLIV, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Jacob D. Cox's The March to the Sea; Franklin and Nashville (1882) is a later history drawing on the official papers; Cox was not in this campaign. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
